text: The Auditor General's Annual Work Plan includes a series of audits along the housing continuum. This series of audits is timely as the City continues to move forward with delivering its priority actions identified in the Homelessness Solutions Service Plan and the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan. Our audit of emergency shelter operations, overseen by the City's Shelter, Support and Housing Administration (SSHA) Division was conducted in several parts. · This report addresses the City's use of hotels to provide emergency shelter. · A separate report addresses the City's delivery of housing case management supports at emergency shelters. SSHA has traditionally contracted with various hotels across the city to supplement its shelter capacity for individuals experiencing homelessness. City Council request the General Manager, Shelter, Support and Housing Administration, in consultation with the Controller, to develop an internal control framework to effectively manage hotel contracts being used to provide emergency shelter services; such internal control framework to include the following measures: a. clear policies and procedures that define the roles and responsibilities for both internal and third-party program staff as well as program support staff who review invoices and authorize payments for hotel shelter services; and b. perform periodic reviews to verify that key contract monitoring and management controls are operating effectively. 2.
